card.title: Mole and its relation with mass, volume and number of particles

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **mole** is chemistry's counting unit: 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number), defined against exactly 12 g of carbon-12. One mole equals the molar mass in grams (n = m/M), contains Nₐ particles (N = nNₐ), and occupies 22.4 L as a gas at STP (n = V/22.4). Molar mass (g/mol) and molecular mass (u) are numerically equal but differ in meaning; a mole is a count, a molecule is a particle.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - n = m/M (mass ↔ moles) - N = n × Nₐ, Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ (particles) - V = n × 22.4 L (gas at STP) - Molar mass M = Σ(atomic masses) in g/mol

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Molar mass (g/mol) vs molecular mass (u):** numerically equal, different units and meaning — one is per mole, the other per molecule.  ·  **Nₐ vs 22.4 L:** Nₐ counts particles in one mole of anything; 22.4 L is the volume of one mole of *gas* at STP only.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The mole is the amount of substance containing as many elementary entities as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***36 g of water*** — 2 mol, 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules (NEB 2023): the classic definition-plus-numerical question.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Chemistry's Currency Converter The **mole** is the SI unit for amount of substance: the amount containing as many elementary entities as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12. One mole = **6.022 × 10²³** particles (Avogadro's number, Nₐ). The mole converts between the three currencies of chemistry: mass (g), volume (L of gas at STP) and number of particles.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The three faces of one mole | Measure | Quantity in 1 mol | Formula | |---|---|---| | **Mass** | Molar mass in grams (H₂O: 18 g) | n = m/M | | **Particles** | 6.022 × 10²³ entities | n = N/Nₐ | | **Gas volume at STP** | 22.4 L | n = V/22.4 | ### 2.2 Worked numericals **Q (NEB 2023, 3m):** What is the mole concept? Calculate the number of molecules in 36 g of water.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Mass/M, Particles/Nₐ, Gas/22.4 — three doors into the mole."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (3m): What is the mole concept? Calculate the number of molecules in 36 g of water.** — Mole: the amount containing as many particles as atoms in exactly 12 g of C-12; 1 mol = 6.022 × 10²³ particles. M(H₂O) = 18 g/mol; n = 36/18 = 2 mol; N = 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ = **1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules**.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In definition questions, quote the carbon-12 standard AND Avogadro's number — both carry marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The mole hop** — every stoichiometric calculation passes through moles: mass → mol → target quantity.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: 1 mol = 6.022 × 10²³ particles = molar mass in grams = 22.4 L of gas at STP. Conversions: n = m/M = N/Nₐ = V/22.4.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Avogadro's number is so large that a mole of marbles would cover the Earth ~50 m deep.
